name: Petra
shortText: The Rose City and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
fullDetails: Petra is an ancient city carved into red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago. It features iconic structures like Al-Khazneh (The Treasury), Ad-Deir (The Monastery), the Siq canyon, and a Roman-style theater.

name: Wadi Rum
shortText: The Valley of the Moon, famous for red sand dunes and starry night camps.
fullDetails: Wadi Rum is a protected desert wilderness featuring dramatic sandstone mountains, ancient Thamudic rock inscriptions, jeep safaris, camel rides, and luxury desert dome camps under clear starry skies.

name: Dead Sea
shortText: The lowest point on Earth, renowned for natural floating and mineral mud.
fullDetails: Located over 430 meters below sea level, the Dead Sea offers a unique natural buoyancy experience due to its high salt concentration. Its mineral-rich mud and luxury thermal resorts make it a premier wellness destination.

name: Roman Theater
shortText: A restored 2nd-century Roman theater in the heart of downtown Amman.
fullDetails: Built during the reign of Antoninus Pius, this 6,000-seat amphitheater is cut into the hillside of downtown Amman. It remains a central cultural venue and houses the Jordan Museum of Popular Traditions.

name: Amman Citadel
shortText: Historic hilltop site with ruins from the Bronze Age to the Umayyad era.
fullDetails: Situated on the highest hill in Amman, the Citadel features the massive columns of the Temple of Hercules, the Byzantine Church, and the grand Umayyad Palace complex, offering panoramic city views.

name: Jerash Archaeological Site
shortText: One of the best-preserved Greco-Roman cities in the world.
fullDetails: Known as the Pompeii of the East, Jerash features remarkable Roman architecture including Hadrian's Arch, the Oval Plaza, the Colonnaded Street, temples, and two grand ancient theaters.

name: Ajloun Castle
shortText: A 12th-century Ayyubid fortress built atop Mount 'Auf.
fullDetails: Built in 1184 AD by one of Saladin's generals, Ajloun Castle protected trade routes and iron mines against Crusaders. It overlooks green pine forests and offers views stretching across the Jordan Valley.

name: Ajloun Cable Car
shortText: A scenic 2.5 km aerial ride over Ajloun's lush green forests.
fullDetails: Jordan's first cable car system connects Ishtafina forest park to Ajloun Castle. It offers passengers breathtaking 360-degree aerial views of the surrounding mountains and pine tree reserves.

name: Umm Qais
shortText: Ancient Decapolis city with views over the Sea of Galilee.
fullDetails: Famous for its black basalt Roman ruins, Western Theater, and Ottoman village. The site provides a magnificent cliffside lookout over the Sea of Galilee, Golan Heights, and Mount Hermon.

name: Karak Castle
shortText: A massive Crusader stronghold with underground passages and vaults.
fullDetails: Standing high on a plateau in southern Jordan, Kerak Castle is a prime example of Crusader military architecture. It features extensive dark stone hallways, subterranean passageways, and defensive towers.

name: Aqaba Marine Reserve
shortText: Red Sea marine park famous for vibrant coral reefs and dive sites.
fullDetails: Protecting 7 km of Red Sea coastline, Aqaba Marine Reserve is home to diverse coral gardens, colorful marine life, and famous diving wrecks such as the Cedar Pride ship and military tank.

name: Ma'in Hot Springs
shortText: Natural thermal mineral waterfalls cascading from mountain cliffs.
fullDetails: Situated 264 meters below sea level, these natural thermal waterfalls reach temperatures up to 60°C. Rich in minerals like hydrogen sulfide and potassium, they are widely known for therapeutic baths.

name: Wadi Mujib
shortText: An exhilarating water canyoning trail through a deep river gorge.
fullDetails: The lowest nature reserve on Earth features a spectacular river canyon entering the Dead Sea. Visitors hike, wade, and climb upstream through rushing waters to reach a dramatic natural waterfall.

name: Madaba Mosaic Map
shortText: The oldest surviving floor map of the Holy Land made of mosaic tiles.
fullDetails: Located inside the 19th-century Greek Orthodox Church of St. George, this 6th-century Byzantine mosaic floor map depicts Jerusalem and the Holy Land with millions of vibrant natural stone pieces.

name: Mount Nebo
shortText: Holy mountain site where Moses viewed the Promised Land.
fullDetails: A revered religious sanctuary elevated 810 meters above sea level. It houses a modern church structure preserving ancient Byzantine mosaics and offers sweeping views of the Dead Sea, West Bank, and Jerusalem.

name: Baptism Site (Al-Maghtas)
shortText: UNESCO World Heritage site identified as the baptism location of Jesus.
fullDetails: Located on the eastern bank of the Jordan River, this holy site encompasses Roman and Byzantine churches, baptismal pools, and caves associated with John the Baptist and the baptism of Jesus.

name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
shortText: Jordan's largest nature reserve spanning four eco-geographical zones.
fullDetails: Dana covers 320 square kilometers of dramatic mountains and valleys. It shelters rare plant species, Nubian ibex, and Syrian serin birds, making it a world-famous destination for eco-tourism and hiking.

name: Shobak Castle
shortText: A remote 12th-century Crusader castle perched on a conical hill.
fullDetails: Built by King Baldwin I of Jerusalem in 1115 AD, Shobak Castle features dramatic ramparts, secret subterranean water tunnels, and inscriptions from Mamluk restorations cut into its perimeter walls.

name: Azraq Wetland Reserve
shortText: An oasis wetland reserve in the heart of Jordan's eastern desert.
fullDetails: A unique desert wetland that serves as a vital stopover for migratory birds flying between Africa and Eurasia. It features wooden boardwalk hides, marshy pools, and native Killifish species.

name: Shaumari Wildlife Reserve
shortText: Breeding center for endangered desert wildlife like the Arabian Oryx.
fullDetails: Established in 1975, Shaumari is dedicated to reintroducing extinct and endangered desert animals. Visitors can take guided open-top safari tours to view Arabian Oryx, ostriches, and Persian wild asses.

name: Desert Castles
shortText: Early Islamic palaces and caravanserais scattered in the eastern plains.
fullDetails: Built during the 7th and 8th centuries by Umayyad Caliphs, these sites include Quseir 'Amra (a UNESCO site famous for wall frescoes) and Qasr al-Kharanah, serving as hunting lodges and desert retreats.

name: The Jordan Museum
shortText: Jordan's primary national museum showcasing 1.5 million years of history.
fullDetails: Located in downtown Amman, the museum presents Jordan's rich heritage through interactive displays, ancient statues of 'Ain Ghazal, and copper scroll copies from the Dead Sea Scrolls collection.

name: Rainbow Street
shortText: A vibrant cultural street lined with cafes, heritage houses, and shops.
fullDetails: One of Amman's most iconic historic streets, offering stone-paved walkways, vintage architecture, cozy coffee shops, rooftop restaurants, art galleries, and weekend artisan markets.

name: Wadi Hasa
shortText: A long, lush canyon featuring flowing river streams and hanging gardens.
fullDetails: A scenic river canyon carved through sandstone formations. It is famous among hikers for its warm flowing water, natural rock pools, hanging moss waterfalls, and palm tree vegetation.

name: Dibbeen Forest Reserve
shortText: The southernmost natural pine-oak forest in the Middle East.
fullDetails: Spanning 8.5 square kilometers of rolling hills, Dibbeen protects ancient Aleppo Pine and oak trees. It provides a peaceful sanctuary for endangered species like the Persian Squirrel and is popular for nature picnics.

name: Wadi Al-Hidan
shortText: A dramatic basalt water canyon with natural pools and waterfalls.
fullDetails: Located in Madaba governorate, Wadi Al-Hidan is a black basalt canyon fed by natural springs. It offers thrilling water hiking, natural swimming pools, and cascading waterfalls surrounded by unique geology.

name: Qasr Al-Mushatta
shortText: The largest and most grand Umayyad winter palace in Jordan.
fullDetails: Situated near Queen Alia International Airport, Qasr Al-Mushatta was constructed by Caliph Walid II in the 8th century. It features impressive stone walls, vaulted halls, and intricate early Islamic architectural carvings.

name: King of Bahrain Forest (Ghamadan)
shortText: A popular pine forest park for outdoor picnics and leisure.
fullDetails: Located in Ghamadan south of Amman, this expansive pine forest serves as a primary outdoor escape for local families. It features shaded picnic areas, walking paths, equestrian clubs, and children's play zones.

name: Royal Automobile Museum
shortText: A unique collection of rare historic cars and motorcycles.
fullDetails: Located in King Hussein Park, this museum displays the private vehicle collection of the late King Hussein and King Abdullah II, highlighting modern Jordanian history through rare classic automobiles, sports cars, and motorbikes.

name: The Royal Tank Museum
shortText: A world-class museum displaying over 110 historic tanks and armored vehicles.
fullDetails: Located in King Abdullah II Park in Amman, the Royal Tank Museum is a specialized military museum. It showcases over 110 historic tanks and armored vehicles, presenting Jordan’s military history alongside global armored warfare developments through interactive exhibits.

name: Afra Hot Springs (Hammat Afra)
shortText: Natural mineral hot springs flowing through deep red canyons.
fullDetails: Afra Hot Springs emerge from over 15 thermal water sources in southern Jordan. The mineral-rich warm waters are renowned for treating skin and joint conditions while flowing naturally through scenic sandstone gorges.
